glossary.entries.circuit.body.0: A circuit wired once and run on every row of a truth table: it outputs the sentence’s value on that row.
glossary.entries.circuit.title: Truth circuits
glossary.groups.logic.title: Logic
level.g-and.intro.0.t: <part-ref to="part:gAnd"></part-ref> outputs true only when both inputs are true.
level.g-and.tasks.g-and.brief: Wire a board that works out the value of “it rains and it is not windy” on every row.
level.g-and.tasks.g-and.hint.0: Two things must hold at once.
level.g-and.title: Rain, but no wind
level.g-not.intro.0.t: A <wiki-ref to="circuit"></wiki-ref> is wired once, and the machine runs it on every row. <part-ref to="part:gNot"></part-ref> stands for negation, ¬.
level.g-not.tasks.g-not.brief: Wire a board that works out the value of “it is not the case that it is not raining” on every row.
level.g-not.tasks.g-not.hint.0: How is “it is not raining” wired? And negated once more?
level.g-not.title: Not not raining
level.g-or.intro.0.t: “Or” is written ∨: true when at least one side is. The prover has no gate for it yet.
level.g-or.tasks.g-or.brief: Using only And and Not, work out the value of “it rains or it is windy” on every row.
level.g-or.tasks.g-or.hint.0: Look first at when it is false: only one row of the four.
level.g-or.title: Rain or wind
level.g-use.intro.0.t: The <part-ref to="lemma:gOr"></part-ref> gate you built is a part now.
level.g-use.tasks.g-use.brief: Work out the value of “it rains or it is windy, and it is cold” on every row.
level.g-use.title: Cold and wet
piece.allE.desc: Connect ∀x. P(x) and choose an object t to obtain P(t).
piece.allE.inputs.0.label: ∀x. P(x)
piece.allE.name: Choose an instance
piece.allI.desc: Name an arbitrary object a on the part. Prove P(a) inside the box and connect it to “Conclusion” to obtain ∀x. P(x) outside. a must not occur in any open assumption.
piece.allI.name: For-any box
piece.allI.regions.0.label: Inside
piece.andE.desc: Connect A ∧ B to get A and B at separate outputs.
piece.andE.inputs.0.label: A ∧ B
piece.andE.name: Split
piece.andE.outputs.0.label: A
piece.andE.outputs.1.label: B
piece.andI.desc: Connect A and B to get A ∧ B.
piece.andI.inputs.0.label: A
piece.andI.inputs.1.label: B
piece.andI.name: Join
piece.anyR.name: Any conclusion
piece.append.desc: Every region receives the same state; gives the result of the first region that does not fail. The number of regions is chosen on the part.
piece.append.name: Alternatives
piece.append.regions.0.label: Try first
piece.append.regions.1.label: Then
piece.append.regions.2.label: Then
piece.append.regions.3.label: Then
piece.append.regions.4.label: Then
piece.append.regions.5.label: Then
piece.assumption.desc: Unifies the first goal with one of its hypotheses: on success the goal is closed and its ?-letters are fixed. It searches from the top and uses the first that fits.
piece.assumption.name: Assumption
piece.botE.desc: From the contradiction ⊥, gives whatever sentence is chosen on the part.
piece.botE.name: Explosion
piece.consFront.desc: Puts “This” at the front of “A list”; when what comes into “A list” is not a list, makes a list of the two.
piece.consFront.inputs.0.label: This
piece.consFront.inputs.1.label: A list
piece.consFront.name: Put first
piece.defer.desc: Moves the first goal to the end; the second becomes the first.
piece.defer.name: Defer
piece.each.desc: The parts inside run once on each goal, seeing only that goal each time; if any goal fails, the whole part fails.
piece.each.name: Each goal in turn
piece.each.regions.0.label: Each goal in turn
piece.eachOf.desc: Wire in a list: the frame receives one item at a time, and its inner output goes to “Result”; each item is processed once, and the results form a list in the original order.
piece.eachOf.name: For each
piece.eachOf.regions.0.label: Each item
piece.exE.desc: Connect ∃x. P(x) and name the existing object a on the part. Inside the box, P(a) may be assumed. Prove C and connect it to “Conclusion” to obtain C outside. a must not appear in C or in any open assumption.
piece.exE.inputs.0.label: ∃x. P(x)
piece.exE.name: Instance box
piece.exE.regions.0.label: Inside
piece.exI.desc: Connect P(t) to obtain ∃x. P(x), with t as a witness. If exactly one existential statement fits, it is selected automatically; if several fit, choose the conclusion on the part.
piece.exI.inputs.0.label: P(t)
piece.exI.name: Generalise
piece.gAnd.desc: a ∧ b: outputs true only when both inputs are true; otherwise false.
piece.gAnd.name: And ∧
piece.gNot.desc: ¬a: true in gives false out; false in gives true out.
piece.gNot.name: Not ¬
piece.gOr.desc: a ∨ b: outputs true when at least one input is true.
piece.gOr.name: Or ∨
piece.impI.desc: A box, with A set on the part. Inside, A may be used as an assumption; prove B there and wire it to “Conclusion”, and the part gives A → B.
piece.impI.name: Assumption box
piece.impI.regions.0.label: Inside
piece.keepBound.desc: Wire in a rule. If it begins with bound variables (⋀x. …), the frame works on the rule after them, and the output keeps the same bound variables in front; if it has none, the frame works on the input itself.
piece.keepBound.name: Keep ⋀
piece.keepBound.regions.0.label: The rule after the bound variables
piece.mkRule.desc: Builds the rule ⟦premises⟧ ⟹ conclusion from premises (a list or a single item) and a conclusion. A sentence is a premise as it is; a rule becomes a premise with its own assumptions.
piece.mkRule.inputs.0.label: Premises
piece.mkRule.inputs.1.label: Conclusion
piece.mkRule.name: Make a rule
piece.mp.desc: From A → B and A, gives B.
piece.mp.inputs.0.label: A → B
piece.mp.inputs.1.label: A
piece.mp.name: Apply
piece.natInd.desc: Two boxes, proving the ∀x. P(x) chosen on the part. The first proves P(0); in the second the number is called a (named on the part; it must not occur in any open assumption), P(a) may be used as an assumption, and P(S a) is to be proved. Once both are proved, the part gives ∀x. P(x).
piece.natInd.name: Mathematical induction
piece.natInd.regions.0.label: The case 0
piece.natInd.regions.1.label: From a to S a
piece.orE.desc: Connect A ∨ B and assume A and B in separate boxes. When both prove the same C and connect it to their respective “Conclusion” ports, the part outputs C.
piece.orE.inputs.0.label: A ∨ B
piece.orE.name: Case analysis
piece.orE.regions.0.label: Case one
piece.orE.regions.1.label: Case two
piece.orI.desc: Connect A and choose another statement B and its position to get A ∨ B or B ∨ A. B need not be proved.
piece.orI.inputs.0.label: A
piece.orI.name: Add alternative
piece.oracle.desc: A fast prover: it cancels all complementary literals between two clauses at once, round after round until ⊥ appears or no new clause does. It too records the two parents of each new clause.
piece.oracle.name: Someone else’s prover
piece.raa.inputs.0.label: ¬¬A
piece.raa.name: By contradiction
piece.refl.desc: Choose a thing t on the part; gives t = t.
piece.refl.name: Reflexivity
piece.repeat.desc: The frame receives the input; its inner output goes to “Result” and back into the frame, round after round, until it stops changing, and the last round’s result is given. If a round fails, it stops at the round before.
piece.repeat.name: Repeat frame
piece.repeat.regions.0.label: Each round
piece.replay.desc: When the clause set contains ⊥, the steps to ⊥ go to the kernel: each input clause used must come from a hypothesis, and each step must be proved from its two parents (variables instantiated by unification) by Own auto. If all pass, the goal the clauses came from is proved; otherwise it names the failing step.
piece.replay.name: Replay
piece.resolve.desc: Tries every pair of clauses in the set once: when a literal of one unifies with the complement of a literal of the other, that pair is cancelled and the remaining literals form a new clause, added with a record of its two parents. Tautologies and duplicates are dropped. It can be set to resolve only against one-literal clauses.
piece.resolve.name: A round of resolution
piece.rewrite.desc: Wire in s = t and a sentence containing s; the part marks each s in it, and the ticked ones become t.
piece.rewrite.inputs.0.label: s = t
piece.rewrite.inputs.1.label: φ(s)
piece.rewrite.name: Substitute equals
piece.rule.desc: Takes rules at its “Rules” port and uses the first that applies: the first goal is unified with the rule’s conclusion and replaced by its premises (one goal per premise, each premise’s own assumptions added to the hypotheses). Any ?-letter not yet fixed stays in the goals.
piece.rule.inputs.1.label: Rule
piece.rule.name: Apply a rule backwards
piece.rw.desc: Takes rewrite rules: in the first goal, outside in and left to right, the first place that fits the rule’s left side becomes its right side, that place alone. A rule with conditions adds each as a new goal after this one. Given several, it uses the first that fits; if nothing fits, it fails.
piece.rw.inputs.1.label: Rule
piece.rw.name: Rewrite
piece.search.desc: Depth-first search: the parts inside take one step on the state received, then go on from each result; each path is followed to its end before backtracking to the next, until no goal remains. Gives every finished state it finds. A step back to where it was (no fewer goals, no more hypotheses) is not followed. A depth limit can be set on the part.
piece.search.name: Backtracking search
piece.search.regions.0.label: Each step
piece.skolem.desc: Removes every ∃ from the first goal’s hypotheses: one with no ∀ outside is taken out as the instance box does; one under a ∀ becomes a new function of all the enclosing ∀ variables (sk1(x) …). The hypotheses must be in negation normal form first.
piece.skolem.name: Skolemise
piece.swapConcl.desc: Wire in a rule and a sentence: keeps the rule’s premises and makes the sentence its conclusion.
piece.swapConcl.inputs.0.label: Rule
piece.swapConcl.inputs.1.label: Becomes
piece.swapConcl.name: Swap conclusion
piece.toClauses.desc: The first goal must be ⊥: its hypotheses are split into clauses. Each must be in CNF; conjunctions are split, each disjunction becomes a clause, ∀s are dropped and variables read as universally quantified.
piece.toClauses.name: Extract clauses
piece.uCheck.desc: Finds ?A ≐ t where t contains ?A and is not ?A itself, and reports failure.
piece.uCheck.name: Occurs check
piece.uConflict.desc: Finds an equation with no ?-letter on either side and different structures (an “and” against an “or”, two different sentences …) and reports failure.
piece.uConflict.name: Conflict
piece.uDecompose.desc: Finds an equation whose sides have the same structure (both “and”, the same predicate …) and splits it into equations between corresponding parts: ?A ∧ ?B ≐ it rains ∧ it is windy becomes ?A ≐ it rains and ?B ≐ it is windy. ¬A splits as A → ⊥.
piece.uDecompose.name: Decompose
piece.uDelete.desc: Finds an equation with identical sides, t ≐ t, and deletes it.
piece.uDelete.name: Delete
piece.uEliminate.desc: Finds ?A ≐ t (t free of ?A) where ?A still occurs in other equations, and replaces ?A with t there.
piece.uEliminate.name: Eliminate
piece.uPattern.desc: Finds ⋀x. ?P(x) ≐ t where ?P is applied to distinct variables bound by the ⋀ and t contains no other ⋀ variable, and solves ?P ≐ fun x => t. When ?P is applied to anything else (?P(ann), ?P(?t)), the equation is left unchanged.
piece.uPattern.name: Pattern unification
piece.uSwap.desc: Finds an equation with a ?-letter on the right only, t ≐ ?A, and turns it into ?A ≐ t.
piece.uSwap.name: Orient
piece.refl.settings.t.label: Which thing
piece.resolve.settings.unit.label: Cancel with
piece.orI.settings.other.label: Other side
piece.orI.settings.side.label: Other side goes
piece.orI.settings.side.options.0.label: Left
piece.orI.settings.side.options.1.label: Right
piece.natInd.settings.P.label: Prove
piece.natInd.settings.x.label: Name
piece.rewrite.settings.at.label: Replace at
piece.allI.settings.x.label: Name
piece.allE.settings.t.label: Which thing
piece.search.settings.depth.label: At most
piece.exI.settings.target.label: Conclusion to derive
piece.botE.settings.C.label: Conclude
piece.rw.settings.at.label: Where
piece.rw.settings.at.options.0.label: Goal
piece.rw.settings.at.options.1.label: Hypotheses
piece.exE.settings.x.label: Witness
piece.append.settings.ways.label: Regions
piece.impI.settings.A.label: Assume
